units.text: EXT. FROZEN RIVER GORGE - DUSK
A slot of black rock, ice-glazed.
Wind scours the canyon floor.
Snow hisses along the ridge like sand.
At the bottom, half under an overhang, a collapsed tent: orange nylon sagging under a week of drift.
Beside it, a dead stove and a rope tied to nothing.

DR. WILHELMINA OSEI-STRAND (40s, glaciologist, frostbitten cheeks, a parka two sizes too big) crouches beside her younger colleague, TOMAS BRENNAN-ADEYEMI (20s, field assistant, one boot missing), who sits propped against the rock with his eyes half open.
Talk to me. Count backward from ten.
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: Ten. Nine.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Keep going.
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: Eight. Tired.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: She tucks her scarf around his throat.
Stands.
Cups her mouth toward the ridge.
Anyone! Anyone up there!
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: Only the wind answers.
She lowers her hands.
Mutters, barely audible.
Okay. Okay. Think. Fire. Heat. Water.
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: She digs through the wreck of the tent and finds a single flare, cracked at the base.
She weighs it in her glove.
We've got one shot. When I say, close your eyes.
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: Why?
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Because I'm going to try to be a lighthouse.
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: She strikes.
The flare sputters, catches.
Red light floods the walls of the gorge, and the falling snow turns to rubies.
Far above, a faint, answering glow.
